correctness.rationale: For all n>=3 and all 0<=u<v<n, an explicit two-effective-merger witness ab^kab^t reaches the prescribed omitted pair. Its minimum candidate length F over both orientations has an all-letter 1-Lipschitz property on every hole set of size <=2. The a-transitions comprise identity, first-hole creation, hole replacement, and second-hole creation; b is handled by appending a rotation. Since hole count is nondecreasing, every path to two holes remains in this domain, so induction makes F a lower bound against arbitrary words. Closed-form minimization gives the four cases, and an exact enumeration of the four pair types gives the histogram. Independent subset-BFS n=3..15 and potential checks n=3..140 passed; those finite checks do not establish infinite correctness.

originality.rationale: published-finding corpus searches of exact pair-target reaching thresholds, adjacent omitted states, and the full Černý distance histogram found related but mathematically weaker extrema and existence results. The three closest published-finding corpus primary RESULT.md files were read. Zhu 2024 and Casas–Volkov 2023 concern general reaching upper bounds and standardized automata; Ferens–Szykuła 2022 and Hoffmann 2020 also do not give this target-indexed formula. The new claim is the explicit value for each omitted pair and the full multiplicity law, not the known upper bound 2n or minimum rank-two deficiency 4. Remaining risks concern unindexed equivalents and possibly older unpublished subset-image computations.
residual_risks: An equivalent individual-reaching-distance function could occur in older transformation-monoid literature not indexed by current search systems.
The accessible 2026 ACM paper cites a four-state example and states a cardinality bound; its entire scholarly full text was not separately inspected beyond accessible text and retrieved summaries.
Originality is best-knowledge, not a claim of independent literature certification.

value.rationale: A prescribed-subset reaching distance, rather than a minimum or maximum over targets, is a canonical quantitative invariant in completely reachable automata and directly refines Don-type bounds. The theorem completely determines all n(n-1)/2 image targets of codimension two for every n, including sharp adjacent-hole obstructions, the full sequence of attained lengths, and target multiplicities. It is not a trivial restatement of the existing 2n bound, the minimum deficiency value 4, or the unique worst k-avoiding target.
